summary.text: You asked the agent to stop refunds from failing when the payment provider times out. It added retries with backoff and a `refund_attempts` table, and reported that all 212 tests pass.
did: Retried timed-out refunds up to 3 times, 2 s, 4 s and 8 s apart
Added the `refund_attempts` table and its migration
Removed the duplicate-refund check from the webhook handler, calling it redundant
summary.state: Everything is committed on `fix/refund-timeouts` (4 commits). The migration has not run against staging.

items.title: A late webhook can now refund a customer twice
items.body: The agent removed the check that stopped the webhook handler from refunding an order that was already refunded, calling it redundant with the new retries. It isn't: when a retry succeeds and the provider's original webhook arrives afterwards, nothing stops a second refund. No test covers a late webhook.

options.label: Restore the check and add a test
options.prompt: In payments/webhooks.py, restore the check that skips a refund when the order already has a successful refund (it was removed in the refund-timeouts work). Add a test where a retry succeeds and then the provider's original webhook arrives late; it must not issue a second refund.

options.label: Explain it to me first
options.prompt: Walk me through what happens when a refund retry succeeds and the provider's original webhook arrives late, with file and line references.

items.title: The migration locks the orders table
items.body: The migration adds a foreign key from `refund_attempts` to `orders` in one step. On Postgres that locks `orders` for writes while it validates every row: about 4 million rows in production. The agent tested it on an empty local database only.

options.label: Add the key as NOT VALID, validate later
options.prompt: Change migration 0042 to add the orders foreign key with NOT VALID, and add a separate migration that runs VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, so the orders table isn't locked during the deploy.

options.label: Run it in a quiet hour as is

items.title: Retries stop after 14 seconds, not after 3 tries
items.body: You asked for "up to 3 retries". The agent also added a 14-second total limit, so on a slow provider only 2 retries may happen. That's reasonable, but it's a policy you didn't choose.

options.label: Remove the time limit
options.prompt: Remove the 14-second total limit on refund retries in payments/refunds.py so it always makes up to 3 retries.

items.title: The test suite does pass
items.body: I re-ran it: 212 passed in 41 s on the branch, matching the agent's report. The 9 new tests cover the retry timing well.

items.title: Nobody has refunded against the provider's sandbox
items.body: Every retry test uses a fake provider. Whether the real sandbox returns the timeout error the code expects (`ProviderTimeout`) hasn't been tried.

question.text: A refund times out, the agent's retry succeeds, and then the provider's original webhook arrives late. What happens now?

choices.text: The webhook is ignored, because the refund already went through.
choices.note: Nothing ignores it any more: the check that did that was removed in this session.

choices.text: The retry is undone and the refund is marked as failed.
choices.note: A late webhook doesn't undo anything. The handler treats it as a new request to refund.

choices.text: `refund_attempts` sees the earlier attempt and blocks the second refund.
choices.note: `refund_attempts` only records attempts. Nothing reads it before issuing a refund.

question.explanation: The retry already issued the refund. When the late webhook arrives, the handler no longer checks whether a refund exists, so it issues another one.

path.text: The retry succeeds and the refund is issued
The provider's original webhook arrives late
The handler no longer checks for an existing refund

question.why: That's why the first call in this briefing matters: restoring the check is a two-line change.
